The study found that performance in selection processes does not predict performance as a dental student. Specifically, the data showed that socio-demographic differences in pre-admission test scores did not affect performance in the dental program.

In other words, while certain factors may influence an individual's initial academic or clinical abilities, these factors do not necessarily translate to success in the dental program. Other factors such as USMLE Step 2 scores, honors in medical school clerkships, and AOA membership are found to be stronger predictors of resident performance.

This study highlights the importance of considering multiple factors when evaluating potential candidates for dental programs. While selection processes may provide some insight into an individual's potential, they should not be relied upon as the sole determining factor in selecting dental students.
